questions.q: In a real close process, why does a team repeatedly refresh the same Smart View workbook rather than each person rebuilding their own version?
options: Rebuilding is actually required by Oracle Fusion
A shared workbook stays the single source of truth; only the underlying numbers change as subledgers close and refresh is clicked
Refreshing deletes the previous period's data permanently
Smart View does not allow more than one refresh per workbook ever
questions.explain: Treating refresh as a team habit keeps one shared workbook current as Payables, Receivables, and GL close in turn, rather than duplicating effort.

questions.q: What does "importing" mean in the context of Smart View and Excel?
options: Uploading a locally built workbook to the Financial Reporting Center
Converting a workbook into a BI Publisher template
Scheduling a report through Enterprise Scheduler Service
Pulling metadata or data from the connected Fusion environment into a worksheet
questions.explain: Importing is the operation that brings Fusion data or metadata into the worksheet, the core of ad hoc Smart View analysis.

questions.q: What is a drawback of distributing a finished Smart View workbook only as a static Excel file?
options: Static files cannot be opened in Excel at all
Static files are automatically deleted after one day
Static distribution is not technically possible
It will go stale the moment the next period closes, since it is only a snapshot as of the last refresh
questions.explain: A static snapshot is fine for one-time distribution but does not stay current the way a published, refreshable workbook would.

questions.q: How does Smart View's distribution model fundamentally differ from BI Publisher's?
options: They are identical in every respect
Smart View can only ever be used by one person at a time
BI Publisher cannot be scheduled, only Smart View can
Smart View's model assumes a human is actively building, reviewing, or refreshing content; BI Publisher's model is built for unattended, scheduled automation
questions.explain: Smart View is designed around interactive, judgment-driven work, while BI Publisher is designed around precise, repeatable, unattended delivery.

questions.q: For a Report Package specifically, what ensures the final version reaches its audience with a documented approval trail?
options: Simply emailing the draft to everyone
Refreshing the workbook one additional time
Publishing through the Narrative Reporting sign-off workflow
Converting it into an OTBI dashboard
questions.explain: The sign-off workflow from the Report Packages lesson is specifically what creates and preserves the documented approval trail before distribution.
